message.reasoning:
I am evaluating the Monopoly jail decision.

I have $818 and two GOOJF cards. The opponent has $395 and no GOOJF cards. I am weighing the cost of the $50 fine against rolling for doubles or using a card.

I will keep both GOOJF cards. I am also checking my housing strategy: pinks are 3/3/4 and oranges are 4/4/4, with zero houses on the bank.

Staying in jail is strategically valuable in the late game. I can collect rent without landing on opponent properties. The opponent's reds are heavily upgraded, with Illinois at four houses and rents around $1100.

I am mapping the board positions. The opponent sits at Income Tax, and I am checking how many spaces remain before they reach my orange and pink properties.

The opponent's next roll from Income Tax would land on Oriental Avenue and Vermont Avenue. Both are mortgaged and rent-free.

A roll of seven or higher from Income Tax would land the opponent on St. Charles, States, Virginia, and St. James. These are my pink and orange properties with three to four houses. The probability of rolling seven or higher is 58 percent. Standard pink rent is 14/14/16.

I am correcting the standard Monopoly rent tables. St. Charles and States are $10/50/150/450/625/750. Virginia is $12/60/180/500/700/900. St. James and Tennessee are $14/70/200/550/750/950. New York is $16/80/220/600/800/1000. Kentucky and Indiana are $18/90/250/700/875/1050. Illinois is $20/100/300/750/925/1100.

I will rely on my own consistent rent notes rather than standard tables. If I leave jail, my roll would land on Electric, States, Virginia, and St. James. Penn RR is mortgaged and rent-free.

Leaving jail would land on Tennessee and New York, then Free Parking, then Kentucky with three houses for roughly seven hundred dollars. Only about eight percent of rolls from jail hit Kentucky immediately. The opponent is still circling the board from Income Tax.

A roll of seven from Income Tax would land the opponent on St. Charles with three houses and rent around four hundred fifty dollars. That exceeds their three hundred ninety-five dollars in cash, forcing them to sell red houses. This is the intended win condition: force the opponent to sell red houses, then buy those houses back immediately. I will stay in jail and roll for doubles.

I will reply briefly to the opponent's taunt. I am recording my reasoning in private notes. Unmortgaging properties or passing GO would not help while the bank holds zero houses.
